title: The Social Construction of Reality in Ethnography
text:
This concept posits that what a society accepts as factual or natural is, in fact, built through ongoing human interaction and language. Instead of mirroring an objective external truth, reality is molded by shared understandings, cultural norms, and institutional frameworks.

The process suggests that social structures—such as gender roles, economic value, or national boundaries—do not exist independently but are rather maintained through collective agreement. Therefore, challenging these foundational agreements can fundamentally alter perceived reality within a given community.
